newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First rejects hands off approach to exporting.
newsitem.headline: NZ First rejects hands off approach to exporting.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said on Thursday his party's policies would give exporters a tail wind rather than the present head wind.

"One is bound to wonder what companies like Power Beat could achieve if they had a governmental tail wind instead of a head wind," he said in notes for a speech tonight at the opening of an electronics assembly centre for battery maker Power Beat.
"New Zealand First's export policy is such a tail wind. We believe in a constructive partnership between government and the export sector," he said.
NZ First holds the balance of power and has been in talks since the October 12 election with the ruling conservative National Party and centre-left Labour Party about forming a coalition.
Peters rejected the current "hands off" approach to exporting.
"There's no such thing as a level playing field in the international market place," he said.
Peters said the October quarter trade deficit was New Zealand's worst ever -- highlighting the dangers of high exchange and interest rates.
